title: MetaCaptioner: Towards Generalist Visual Captioning with Open-source Suites
claim: Our model's output matches the strongest commercial system's quality, while the open-source baseline errs, across many input domains.
layout: Image left, three stacked caption boxes center, metric cards right, domain strip below
description: A dark-background bubble-chart infographic about dark web drug sales sits on the left. Next to it, three rounded text boxes are stacked vertically. The blue one holds GPT-4.1V's caption, the red one OmniCaptioner's caption, and the green one MetaCaptioner's caption. Key phrases are highlighted in bold and color. The red box underlines errors, such as a wrong category count and a '$469 million' figure for Weed. The green box highlights accurate, insightful phrases. Each box has a dashed metric card to its right. The cards rate Factual Accuracy, Professionalism, Information Completeness and Reasoning Rigor as Excellent, Good or Bad. OmniCaptioner gets Bad on two of the four. Along the bottom, a rounded strip holds nine pastel domain boxes, from Natural Perception to Synthetic Image, labeled 'Visual Caption Domains in MetaCaptioner'. Dashed green lines link the strip to the image and to the green box.
caption: Comparison of caption quality between GPT-4.1, OmniCaptioner [ref] and MetaCaptioner. These metrics are computed by GPT-5. MetaCaptioner is able to generate informative captions for a variety of visual domains with comparable quality to GPT-4.1.
abstract: Generalist visual captioning goes beyond a simple appearance description task, but requires integrating a series of visual cues into a caption and handling various visual domains. In this task, current open-source models present a large performance gap with commercial ones, which limits various applications such as data synthesis. To bridge the gap, this paper proposes CapFlow, a novel multi-agent collaboration workflow. CapFlow demonstrates for the first time that, by capitalizing on open-source models, it is possible to achieve caption quality on par with GPT-4.1 in various domains with an 89.5% reduction in costs. By leveraging CapFlow as the data synthesizer, we produce high-quality visual captions from image and video domains at scale, and obtain a generalist visual captioner via fine-tuning, namely MetaCaptioner. Through extensive experiments, we show that MetaCaptioner not only achieves comparable captioning capabilities with commercial models but also reaches top-tier multimodal performance in the open-source community. We hope CapFlow and MetaCaptioner can benefit future multimodal research by providing a strong and cost-effective visual captioning solution.
